sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Rotten Breath** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Dragon Communion:** Caelid / Jagged Peak
- Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid and the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 1 Dragon Heart.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a heavy, rotting mist, dealing Standard damage equal to 131% of Incantation Scaling and causing 65 Scarlet Rot build-up up to 3 times (i.e. damage for 393% of the same and 195 build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 48 points of Stamina to cast, and another 48 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
 - Note that while the Dragon Communion Seal scales with Arcane, Scarlet Rot will not scale with that, so Rotten Breath gains no innate benefit except for the damage boost.
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- Can be cast while mounted but cannot be cast midair, unlike Ekzykes's Decay.
- Compared to Ekzykes's Decay, this spell deals 15% less damage but also consumes 29% less FP.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 120 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*4 FP from keeping the spell running.
 - Only 65 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
- This is the weakest "default" dragon breath attack, but it's also the only one that deals Physical damage.
 - Compatible with the Blue Dancer Charm, even more so since its two primary boosting items, the Dragon Communion Seal and Rock Heart, are weightless.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.
- The Scarlet Rot deals damage roughly equal to 1170 + 29.7% of the target's maximum health over the course of 90 seconds.
 - The total Scarlet Rot build-up is 390 if using both breaths, enough to afflict many vulnerable enemies and bosses with the Status Effect and most non-resistant ones within two full casts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 reduced the Scarlet Rot status effect buildup for Rotten Breath.
 - The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.
 - The status build-up per hit was decreased from 130 to 65 (total build-up reduced from 780 to 390).

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Roundtable Hold** is the main hub area in Elden Ring. Entry to Roundtable Hold is locked until the player receives an invitation from Melina, achieved by resting at a Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes or Caelid, or by defeating Margit, the Fell Omen. Afterward, the Roundtable Hold can be accessed via fast travel from the map.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: A pocket realm tied to the Erdtree's Grace, the Roundtable Hold exists to aid the Tarnished on their quest for the Elden Ring, with Smithing Master Hewg as its foundation. It is a copy of Leyndell's Fortified Manor, once a gathering place for great champions seeking the Two Fingers' divine wisdom. A bustling community of mighty Tarnished likewise convened in the Hold in the distant past; however, it is now a shadow of its former glory, with its present occupants lacking the venerable status and lofty aspirations of those past heroes, such as Vargram the Raging Wolf, Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm, Mad Tongue Alberich, Dolores the Sleeping Arrow, and Roundtable Knight Vyke, who came closest to the title of Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Layout
sections.markdown: Roundtable Hold consists of a main floor and a cellar, each comprised of several rooms. Certain rooms are inaccessible until certain requirements are met.

sections.heading: Lobby
sections.markdown: The central chamber of the Hold, containing the circular Table of Lost Grace site of grace, from which it gets its name. The player shall appear in this chamber every time they visit Roundtable Hold. Brother Corhyn, Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing, and Knight Diallos can all be found here initially, later joined by Roderika, Spirit Tuner and D, Hunter of the Dead. A Marika statue by the fireplace can be used to access the Colosseums, once unlocked.

sections.heading: Northern Wing
sections.markdown: The northern wing, ahead and to the left upon arriving in Roundtable Hold, consists of a corridor which branches into Gideon's study and the Twin Maiden Husks' room. Ensha of the Royal Remains stands guard outside Gideon's study, and Nepheli Loux, Warrior briefly appears here after Godrick the Grafted has been defeated.

sections.heading: Gideon's Study
sections.markdown: A spacious room which has been adapted into a study by Gideon Ofnir, who can usually be found behind his desk. It will be locked upon first visiting Roundtable Hold, but will open either after claiming a Great Rune or talking to Gideon and reloading.

sections.heading: Twin Maiden Husks
sections.markdown: The Twin Maiden Husks can be found in a room through a door in the northern wing. Here, the player can buy and sell various items. They receive Bell Bearings, which allows them to sell the goods of dead merchants. Some of these Bell Bearings carry over into .

sections.heading: Library
sections.markdown: A small library behind a door in the Twin Maiden Husks' room, which will only open after touching a Site of Grace in Altus Plateau. The back of the library is piled with decaying corpses, and is occupied by the spirit of the Dung Eater.

sections.heading: Eastern Wing
sections.markdown: The eastern wing is a corridor which connects to Fia's room, the armory, and the cellar. Smithing Master Hewg resides here, and is later joined by Roderika.

sections.heading: Fia's Room
sections.markdown: A large bedroom occupied by Fia, Deathbed Companion. The Clouded Mirror Stand to the right upon entering can be used to open the Character Creation menu and alter one's appearance.

sections.heading: Balcony
sections.markdown: Situated between the northern and eastern wings, a balcony overlooks the great hall. Sorcerer Rogier retreats here after leaving Stormveil Castle.

sections.heading: Hall
sections.markdown: A large hall lined with banners and statues, accessed by dropping down from the balcony. Mad Tongue Alberich will invade when the player approaches the far end of the hall. After he has been defeated, a wisp of light will appear which allows the player to return to the balcony above.

sections.heading: Living Quarters
sections.markdown: A series of rooms connected to the hall, to the left after dropping down from the balcony. The Cipher Pata can be found on a corpse lying on one of the beds.

sections.heading: Armory
sections.markdown: A locked room at the far end of the eastern wing. It will only open after giving D the Weathered Dagger, received from Fia.

sections.heading: Pantry
sections.markdown: A storage room on the lower level, at the bottom of a flight of stairs past Hewg in the eastern wing. It is initially empty, but Nepheli Loux will move here after the Omenkiller in the Village of the Albinaurics has been defeated.

sections.heading: Dining Room
sections.markdown: A narrow room connected to the pantry, which requires a Stonesword Key to open. There is a treasure chest containing Crepus's Black-Key Crossbow and 20 Black-Key Bolts.

sections.heading: Kitchen
sections.markdown: A room connected to the dining room, requiring two Stonesword Keys to open. A treasure chest contains the Assassin's Prayerbook.

sections.heading: Audience Chamber
sections.markdown: A throne room connected to the lobby, wherein resides the Two Fingers and Finger Reader Enia. This chamber is locked until at least one Great Rune has been obtained. The player comes here to progress the main story and to trade in Remembrances for boss items.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Rotten Winged Sword Insignia** is a talisman in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: - Obtained from Millicent after choosing to assist her in defeating her sisters, as part of her questline.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Increases attack power for every 3 hits landed, with the bonus increasing further for every 3 hits after that for an overall bonus of 6%/8%/13%. Bonus decreases by 1 "tier" every 1.5 seconds that pass without getting a point.

Light attacks count as 1 hit towards this buff and heavy attacks count as 2 hit towards it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Mainly works for melee weapons, with only certain Sorceries (Adula's Moonblade, Gavel of Haima, Carian Greatsword, Carian Piercer, and Carian Slicer) and certain Incantations (Aspects of the Crucible: Tail, Aspects of the Crucible: Horns, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive).
 - These spells counts as a heavy attack, i.e. they count as 2 hits if they land.
 - For spells with a melee component and a ranged component, progress is only granted if the melee component hits. These spells are Adula's Moonblade, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive.
- For Skills it only works if they can hit using the weapon, such as with Skill: Sword Dance, Unique Skill: Eochaid's Dancing Blade, or the melee part of Skill: Blood Blade. Melee range skills that nonetheless don't directly hit with the weapon, such as Skill: Black Flame Tornado don't count.
- Can be worn together with the Millicent's Prosthesis to stack the effect, but not with the Winged Sword Insignia.
 - However, this talisman and the Prosthesis can't be obtained in the same playthrough, instead requiring a new cycle of New Game+ to obtain.
- Light or heavy attacks that hit several times per input counts as hits each time they hit an enemy.
 - An example of this is the unique heavy attack shared by the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger, which hits twice and therefore can count as either 2 or 4 hits depending if it manages to hit once or twice.
 - This also counts for some skills that use heavy attacks and can hit several times, such as the heavy attack follow-up to the Stamp (Sweep) skill and the altered heavy attacks granted by the Barbaric Roar skill.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.markdown: - At some point between an unknown Patch and Patch 1.03.3, this talisman was apparently bugged, with the buff that is applied to attack power both increasing and decreasing with successive attacks. That is, in some scenarios, performing an additional attack within a sequence would cause attack power to decrease, rather than increase. This could be observed when using the Dagger and Short Sword weapons. This effect could be observed for the Winged Sword Insignia as well.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Runes** () act as both the currency and experience points (XP) in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Runes are a main game mechanics behind runes is that they'll be lost on death, and the only way to get them back is to return to the area where they were lost to reclaim them. However, if one should die before they can retrieve the lost runes, they'll be lost permanently.

Runes are gained by defeating enemies, but also exist as Tools, which can be picked up and are sometimes dropped by enemies. These Golden Runes exist in various forms, which provide increasing numbers of runes when used or sold to merchants (for the same number of runes as when used).

sections.heading: Golden Runes
sections.markdown: The various forms of these rune objects, in increasing order of how many runes they provide, are: Golden Rune 1, Golden Rune 2, Golden Rune 3, Golden Rune 4, Golden Rune 5, Golden Rune 6, Golden Rune 7, Golden Rune 8, Lands Between Rune, Golden Rune 9, Golden Rune 10, Golden Rune 11, Golden Rune 12, Golden Rune 13, Numen's Rune, Hero's Rune 1, Hero's Rune 2, Hero's Rune 3, Hero's Rune 4, Hero's Rune 5, Lord's Rune

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Unlike dungeon boss fights, if one dies inside an evergaol, the runes will be retrievable on the surface/entrance area to the evergaol, so there's minimal risk in fighting bosses in evergaols.
- Golden Runes and any other item that grants runes are not lost on death, so it's best to keep them in their object state until ready to level up or buy something to minimize rune losses
- Sacrificial Twigs can be used in a talisman slot, so on the subsequent death, the twig is lost rather than one's runes.
- Remembrances grant runes upon use.
- Gold-Pickled Fowl Foot, Golden Horn Tender, and Gold Scarab boost rune acquisition.
- A Rune bonus multiplier applies anytime a player with the same multiplayer password defeats a Shardbearer or becomes Elden Lord.

A fortress on an island to the south of Caelid, connected to the mainland by a heavily fortified greatbridge. The castle is the stronghold of General Radahn's army, beaten yet unbowed after their defeat at the hands of Malenia and her Cleanrot Knights.

Redmane Castle is also the site of the Radahn Festival; a contest in which great champions attempt to defeat the Rot-maddened Radahn and claim his Great Rune. This event is initiated either by activating a Site of Grace in Altus Plateau or by progressing Ranni the Witch's questline.

During the Radahn Festival, all of the enemies in the castle (except for the two Elder Lions) will disappear, and the boss (if not defeated already) will not show up in the plaza. Once Starscourge Radahn has been defeated, the enemies will return and the boss can be fought if not defeated already.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Roderika, Spirit Tuner**, also known as the **Heartbroken Maiden**, is a merchant character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A Tarnished noblewoman who, despite having never seen the guidance of grace, travelled to the Lands Between along with her companions. After arriving, those companions fell victim to Godrick, becoming subjects for his grafting. Roderika alone survived, taking refuge in Stormhill Shack. It is here that she meets the Tarnished. She beseeches the Tarnished to bring a message to her grafted companions, whom she refers to as chrysalids, assuring them that she loves them and will join them soon.

Roderika then heads to Roundtable Hold. Here, she becomes acquainted with Smithing Master Hewg, who takes notice of her gift for spirit tuning and is reminded of a spirit tuner he knew long ago, whose eyes were of the same hue as Roderika's. Reluctantly, Hewg agrees to teach Roderika everything he knows about spirit tuning.

Roderika remains at Roundtable Hold, where she hones her newfound talent and eventually becomes a fully-fledged spirit tuner. Her ability to sense spirits allows her to notice the Dung Eater's presence, which she warns the Tarnished about.

After the Erdtree burns, Roderika attempts to convince Hewg to leave Roundtable, but to no avail. She chooses to respect Hewg's decision, and remains behind with him even after he forgets her. As the hold burns, she begs the Tarnished to become Elden Lord, and to use the weapons Hewg forged to slay Queen Marika the Eternal.

sections.heading: Spirit Tuning
sections.markdown: Roderika can upgrade Spirit Ashes up to +10 using Grave Glovewort and Ghost Glovewort.

sections.heading: Character information
sections.markdown: Roderika cannot be harmed or killed.

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.markdown:
1. *(Optional)* Stormhill Shack
 - Roderika can be found in Stormhill Shack in Stormhill, provided you have not defeated Godrick the Grafted or touched a Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes. Exhaust her dialogue to obtain both the "Sitting Sideways" Gesture and Spirit Jellyfish Ashes.
1. *(Optional)* Stormveil Castle
 - In an adjoining courtyard to the large hall containing a Grafted Scion in Stormveil Castle, pick up the Chrysalids' Memento.
1. *(Optional)* Stormhill Shack
 - Deliver the Crysalids' Memento to Roderika in Stormhill Shack and exhaust her dialogue to get her to move to Roundtable Hold.
1. Roundtable Hold
 - Roderika can be found by the fireplace in the central room. Talk to her to obtain a Golden Seed once she arrives.
 - **Note**: if you defeated Godrick or rest at a Site of Grace in Liurnia without speaking to Roderika in Stormhill Shack, she will move to Roundtable Hold on her own, and will leave the Golden Seed on the ground in the shack.
1. Roundtable Hold
 - Speak to Roderika, and then speak to Smithing Master Hewg and select "About Roderika".
1. Roundtable Hold
 - Return to Roderika and speak to her to tell her what Hewg said.
1. Roundtable Hold
 - Return to Hewg and select "About Roderika" again, followed by "Would you watch over Roderika?" and finally "It's what she wants".
1. Roundtable Hold
 - Reload the area and Roderika will be sitting opposite Hewg. It is now possible to upgrade Spirit Ashes by speaking to her.
1. *(optional)* Roundtable Hold
 - Upgrade a Spirit Ash to at least +4 and talk to her to receive the "Curtsy" Gesture.
1. Roundtable Hold
 - After burning the Erdtree, return to the Roundtable Hold, speak to Hewg, and select "Let's talk a while". You may then select the dialogue option "Why are you still making weapons?" After talking to Roderika and selecting "About Hewg", return to Hewg and select "What happened to her?"
1. Roundtable Hold

sections.markdown: The **Royal Greatsword** is a Colossal Sword, a melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: Obtained from Blaidd, along with his armor set (except the Black Wolf Mask), when encountered at Ranni's Rise after Ranni the Witch's storyline has been completed. Killing him prior to this will award no items.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The Intelligence-scaling is actually slightly stronger than the Strength-scaling despite having the same letter grade.
 - This means that a pure Intelligence build is the strongest way to build this weapon. However, because scaling values become less effective after reaching 40-50 in a stat and because wielding this weapon already requires a fair investment in Strength, a hybrid Str/Int build has almost as much AR while requiring much fewer Attribute points to do.
- The weapon itself does not cause Frostbite but both parts of the skill, the stab-jump and the explosion, do cause some build-up (60 on the stab and 100 on the explosion).

- Patch 1.07 increased the poise when casting the skill.
- Patch 1.09 increased the scaling values of the weapon.
- As the description implies, this resembles a much more ornate version of the standard Greatsword.
- Shares it name with a weapon from Dark Souls 2 (Royal Greatsword), which was a Greatsword-type weapon and Strength-based counterpart to that game's version of the Flamberge.

sections.markdown: Rotten Crystal Sword** is a straight sword found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: In a treasure chest guarded by three Crystalians in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, behind some large tree roots right after the Ephael Inner Wall grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Effectively just the Crystal Sword but with slight Scarlet Rot build-up, much, much later acquisition, and lower damage from very slightly lower Strength-scaling and lower Physical and Magic base damage.
- The skill, Spinning Slash, is potentially quite damaging, especially if it catches another player offguard and with low Poise, though it's somewhat hampered by the lack of reach on Straight Swords.
- Does best as a pure Strength weapon, as Dexterity and Intelligence are somewhat hampered by having much lower scaling numbers and being based off the lower Magic base damage respectively.
 - For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 80 Strength grants 625 Attack Power (AP), 45 Strength and 45 Intelligence grants 607 AP, 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 599 AP, and 80 Intelligence grants 540 AP.
 - Has on average 25 less AP
- A good offhand weapon for those wishing to dual-wield Straight Swords on a Strength build with some Intelligence, due to the ease of upgrading weapons reliant on Somber Smithing Stones and its somewhat mediocre skill not mattering there.

- The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Rune of Death** (死のルーン, *Shi no Rūn*), also known as **Destined Death** (運命の死, *Unmei no Shi*), is an unobtainable Great Rune in Elden Ring that controls the fated deaths of the Demigods. Once part of the Elden Ring, it was removed by Queen Marika and sealed away when she established her Golden Order. It appears during the cutscene that plays when the player defeats Maliketh, the Black Blade at Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: Destined Death is a crimson, cross-shaped rune with tapered ends, resembling Marika's Rune with a downward arc. Smoke emanates from the rune as a jagged black fissure splits it vertically through its center. It manifests within a font of Darkness upon its unsealing.

sections.heading: Destined Death
sections.markdown:
The Rune of Death can grant Destined Death, or true and fated death. When used to carve the Cursemark of Death in a full ring, it kills the recipient in both body and soul; however, incomplete rings can apply partial effects under specific circumstances. Known as half-wheels of the centipede, the waxing crescent burns away the flesh while the waning crescent destroys only the soul.

The Rune also produces crimson flames with golden motes that inflicts the Destined Death status effect, which reduces maximum HP and deals damage over time. The power of Destined Death could be repelled by the Blasphemous Claw or a depiction of the eclipsed sun.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: The Rune of Death was once embedded within the Elden Ring, empowering the black flames to deliver Destined Death to even gods. It was venerated by the Godskin Apostles and wielded by the Gloam-Eyed Queen, whose sacred Godslayer's Greatsword channeled black flames. The Queen, an Empyrean chosen by the Fingers, led the Apostles on their god hunt; however, she was ultimately vanquished by Maliketh, the shadowbound beast and loyal vassal of Queen Marika.

sections.heading: Golden Order
sections.markdown: With the Gloam-Eyed Queen defeated, Marika extracted the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring, and Maliketh sealed it within his Black Blade. This act was the foundation of the Golden Order and established Marika as the one true god. It exempted the Demigods from dying true deaths, granting them immortality, and also conferred a form of unending life to the Erdtree people. With the true lethality of Godslayer incantations suppressed, only Maliketh held the power to destroy the Demigods, and there was not one among them who did not fear him.

sections.heading: Night of Black Knives
sections.markdown:
At a later point in history, a fragment of the Rune of Death was stolen from Maliketh by Ranni the Witch, who used it to create the godslaying Black Knives through a fearsome rite. On the Night of Black Knives, the Black Knife Assassins used these blades to murder Godwyn the Golden, the first Demigod to perish in all of recorded history. However, due to Ranni carving the Cursemark of Destined Death into her flesh at the same moment as Godwyn's death, he was unable to die a proper death and perished in soul alone. Meanwhile, Ranni's flesh perished and her soul continued to live, inhabiting a doll body. After the Night of Black Knives, Maliketh bound his sword within his own flesh in order to ensure that none would ever steal Death again.

Godwyn was given an Erdtree Burial at the Erdtree's roots in the Deeproot Depths beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital. However, his soulless body soon began a grotesque transformation into the blighted Prince of Death. Fragments of the Rune of Death began to spread through the underground Greattree roots connected to Godwyn's corpse, sprouting in the form of Deathroot, and leading to the rise of Those Who Live in Death.

As Gurranq, Beast Clergyman, Maliketh attempts to reclaim the stolen shards by consuming Deathroot, an endeavor he believes will restore the Golden Order and end his hunger. After devouring all nine Deathroots, his hunger persists and he realizes that the Golden Order cannot be restored. He was, in truth, betrayed by Marika.

Marika's daughter, Melina, aids the Tarnished knowing their quest will ultimately violate the Golden Order. Her purpose as the Kindling Maiden is to commit the Cardinal Sin and unlock the path to Maliketh and Destined Death. Although Maliketh unbinds the Black Blade, he is defeated. The Tarnished interacts with the Rune, unleashing a burst of crimson flame. The Erdtree is engulfed in crimson flames, and its impenetrable thorns are burned away.

If the Tarnished rises as the Lord of Frenzied Flame after using the Frenzied Flame to spare Melina, she gains or unlocks the power of Destined Death.

This is because the damage are incredibly minimal to both normal attacks (maxing out at +32 Magic damage with 99 Intelligence if the weapon is upgraded to +10) and because unlike how these sort of weapons scale normally, where Intelligence provides minimal weapon damage bonuses but great skill damage bonuses, both weapon upgrade level and Strength provide far greater bonuses to the skill's damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The skill, Eochaid's Dancing Blade, is both chargeable (benefiting from the Godfrey Icon) and actually counts for repeated-hits boosters such as the Winged Sword Insignias and Thorny Cracked Tear, something many other repeated-hits skills such as the Ghiza's Wheel's skill Spinning Wheel or the Ornamental Straight Sword's skill Golden Tempering's special heavy attacks don't.
 - It's however somewhat outclassed by the Marais Executioner's Sword when it comes to dealing damage with the skill, as the latter is a Greatsword and thus has greater Attack Power for the skill to be based off.
 - Since the skill's damage is based entirely of off the weapon's base Attack Power, and about a third of the Regalia's damage is Magic damage, Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear and Terra Magica functionally give +7% damage and +12% damage respectively if they can be set up beforehand.
- Though both the Dexterity-scaling and the Arcane-scaling may appear equal, and technically are as both are valued at 0.66, the Arcane-scaling actually applies to BOTH the Physical damage and the Magic damage. This effectively places it as a mid-tier B-scaling (1.08 scaling instead of 0.66 scaling). However, due to scaling falling off around 54 points in a damage stat (see the Weapon Scaling page) a hybrid Dexterity/Arcane build holds up fairly well.
 - For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 80 Arcane grants 631 Attack Power (AP), 45 Dexterity and 45 Arcane grants 618 AP, and 80 Dexterity grants 561 AP.
 - With a pure Arcane build this weapon will outmatch Occult affinity Straight Swords by 90-100 AP. As this is largely due to the innate Magic damage, this can be somewhat misleading in its performance if enemies are resistant to that damage type.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Rya the Scout**, also known as **Zorayas the Scout**, is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
A young woman who works as a scout for the Recusants of Volcano Manor, tasked with recruiting Tarnished to the cause. Rya is the adopted daughter of Tanith, although she believes her to be her true mother. In truth, Rya is a Man-Serpent of Mt. Gelmir, born of a repellent birthing ritual, and her true name is Zorayas.

Rya first encounters the Tarnished in Liurnia of the Lakes, where they assist her in retrieving her Necklace from Blackguard Big Boggart. In return, Rya invites the Tarnished to Volcano Manor, where they have the opportunity to join the Recusants and serve under Tanith. During their service, the Tarnished stumbles upon Rya in her true, serpentine form. Rya reports hearing slithering sounds beyond the walls of the Manor, and begins to question her origins when the Tarnished reveals to her the secrets of the Manor, having previously believed herself to have been born of a king's grace. When the Tarnished presents her with the Serpent's Amnion, which she surmises to have come from her birth mother, she ventures deeper into Volcano Manor to learn the truth behind her birth, hoping to one day be able to call Tanith her mother again.

Concerned about her daughter, Tanith requests that the Tarnished give Rya a Tonic of Forgetfulness, to prevent the distress caused by the truth of her birth.

The Tarnished finds Rya deep within the Manor, where she reveals that she has discovered her origins as the product of a hideous ritual. Distressed, she begs the Tarnished to kill her. Should the Tarnished agree, she will thank the Tarnished and her mother before passing. Should they instead give her the Tonic of Forgetfulness, she will fall asleep, and later return to the Manor's drawing room, with no memories of her journey, still believing Tanith to be her mother.

Should the Tarnished refuse to kill her or give her the tonic, she will leave Volcano Manor, leaving behind a letter declaring her intention to set out on a journey so that she can continue Tanith's work.

Rebirth** (commonly known as *respeccing*) is a mechanic featured in Elden Ring. Allowing the player to allocate points into different Attributes points during the game.

It is unlocked after defeating Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, and is located next to the Raya Lucaria Grand Library Sites of Grace.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Rebirthing requires one Larval Tear.

It is important to note that the players starting origin (I.E. Samurai, Vagabond, or Astrologer) serves as the starting basis in terms of stat allocation for Rebirthing. Meaning that a player who started as a Samurai will have 12 Vigor points invested already while an Astrologer will start with 6 Vigor points. All points earned up to the level the player is currently at must be allocated for rebirth.

If the player chooses to cancel their Rebirthing, they will not lose a Larval Tear.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Regal Omen Bairn** is a reusable tool in *Elden Ring* and a stronger, more costly alternative to the Omen Bairn.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Trade the Remembrance of the Omen King, gained by defeating Morgott, the Omen King, and 5000 Runes with Finger Reader Enia.

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums with a bell to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Using this item will make the player-character brace themselves for a second before unleashing a close-ranged explosion that'll launch human-sized (or smaller) opponents away from them before sending out 10 long-ranged wraith projectiles that'll track any target that the user was locked on to as they were ejected from their body. These wraiths travel in three groups, the first two groups being comprised of 3 projectiles each and the final having 4, each group also have their own defined travel speed, leading to three distinct rolling windows whenever the player is fighting against this tool in PvP.

As it deals Holy Damage; any holy-boosting equipment or spell will further increase the damage from this item.
Each piece of the Omen Set will also increase the damage of this item by 5%, meaning wearing the full set will increase it by 20%.

sections.markdown: - The doll depicts Morgott, the Omen King and was likely made in secret by his father, Godfrey, First Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Soldiers in the service of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, also known as the Cuckoos. They were given free rein by the academy to wage war as they pleased, and they are infamous for their rapacious ways. They wear red-and-blue surcoats bearing a design of two cuckoos peering at a flourishing mass of glintstone, and each of their helms is adorned with a single cuckoo's feather. They are capable of using Cuckoo Glintstone in combat.

When the Academy turned against the Carian Royal Family, the Cuckoos launched an assault on Caria Manor, however they were caught in an enchanted snare. They were turned into spectral puppets, forced to defend the Manor against further invasions.

A detachment of Raya Lucaria Soldiers can be found in the Frenzied Flame Village, having apparently succumbed to Madness.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Royal Revenant** is an enemy and boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Pale, gaunt creatures resembling corpses with many limbs. They emerge from pools of shallow water, and attack with unnatural speed and the ability to inflict Poison.

They are weak to Holy damage, and take damage from and are stunned by healing incantations such as Heal, Great Heal, Lord's Heal and Erdtree Heal, losing half their health if hit. They also take damage from healing over time incantations, such as Blessing's Boon and Blessing of the Erdtree, losing 90% of their health over 30 seconds if affected by such as spell.

They are often accompanied by Revenant Followers.

sections.heading: Bosses
sections.markdown: Kingsrealm Ruins=

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: A Royal Revenant encountered in the hidden cellar of Kingsrealm Ruins in north-western Liurnia of the Lakes. It guards a chest containing the Frozen Needle.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.markdown:
Encountered in a very small room and without having to go through their signature lengthy spawning animation, this Revenant will turn aggressive quickly.

If it leaps towards roll forwards to the left of it and get in a hit before backing away, being ready to roll. Should it start to use more short-ranged melee slams, back away to provoke more leaps. Sometimes it will start to chain these slams into one long combo, either try to keep as far away as possible from this or get behind it if already close.

Occasionally it will start to emit a green color around its head which signifies that it's about to spit out a thin cone of Poison sludge. Potentially dangerous if caught in the middle of an action such as drinking a Flask of Crimson Tears but otherwise easily rolled or jumped away from.

Sometimes it will slip through a portal underground to appear behind its target and spit poison before starting its attack routine again.

sections.heading: Healing incantations
sections.markdown:
One easy way to kill it is to find an opening to cast a cheap healing spell such as Heal and then cast it again immediately while it's stunned. Any class can do this as even a Prisoner has enough Faith with a Commoner's Garb/Commoner's Simple Garb and Two Fingers Heirloom.

Another way to do this is to summon the Finger Maiden Therolina Puppet, though she's more unreliable in casting her healing incantation.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Revenant** (復讐者, *Fukushuusha*, lit. Revenger), also known as the **Night Idol** (夜の偶像, *Yoru no Gūzō*), is a character in Elden Ring Nightreign. She is one of the ten available Nightfarer classes.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: The Revenant is a living doll that joined the Nightfarers to take down the Nightlord.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Revenant is a summoner class that specializes in ranged magic damage.

Revenant is a blue-eyed maiden with porcelain skin and braided white hair. A white veil and a crown of assorted blue flowers rest upon her head. She wears a ghostly white gown, a blue cape, and an assortment of amulets depicting rings. She is often seen playing a lyre while barefoot, and uses a variation of Spirit Ashes system to summon the spirit of a Giant Skeleton.

sections.heading: How to unlock the Revenant
sections.markdown:
The Revenant is not present at the Roundtable Hold at the start of the game. She must be unlocked before she may be selected.

1. Face or defeat the first Nightlord.
1. Purchase Besmirched Frame () from the Small Jar Bazaar.
1. Locate the Revenant's phantom in the room adjacent to the Table of Lost Grace. She stares at a painting of Lord Radagon.
1. Interact with her and select **Yes** to **Touch the phantom**.
1. Player is transported to a Fort in Limveld, directly facing the same painting of Radagon.
1. Travel southeast to the nearby Ruins.
1. Face the Night Idol.
 - She casts Rejection and Triple Rings of Light.
 - Her summoned buddies will not respawn once defeated.
1. Defeating the Night Idol unlocks the Revenant as a playable character.

The following effects are listed in preferred order. Two or more effects on a single relic should be prioritized. If an effect is listed as "Stacks" it means it may be applied to more than one relic and still work.
- [Revenant] Power up while fighting alongside family
- Improved Godslayer/Dragon Cult/Fundamental Incant
- Attack power up after defeating a Night Invader
- Attack Power permanently increased for each Evergaol prisoner defeated
- [Fire/Lightning/Holy] Attack Power Up (Stacks)
- Improves [Incantation Type] (Stacks)
- [Revenant] Strengthens families and allies when ultimate art is activated
- Wraith Calling Bell in possession at start of game
- [Revenant] Trigger ghostflame explosion during Ultimate Art activation
- Defeating enemies fills more of the Art gauge
- Vigor +3 (Stacks)
- Flask also heals nearby allies
- Item confer effect to all nearby allies

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: - Once unlocked, the Revenant is present at the Shrouded Roundtable Hold if she is not selected as the player character.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Collecting the Revenant as a playable character for the first time unlocks the "The Revenant Joins the Fray" achievement.
- Revenant's spirit buddies benefit from effects applied to nearby allies, such as the Flask Also Heals Allies bonus provided by the Night of the Fathom.
- The Necromancy passive can work on some mini-bosses, such as Banished Knights, Mad Pumpkin Heads, etc.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Revenant was the last of the eight heroes revealed on April 30, 2025.
- Among the Nightfarers, the Revenant stands as the shortest.
- Her name as a doll, Daphne, is Greek for "laurel".
- Although all Nightfarers have custom movesets with their preferred weapon types, the Revenant is the only one with a moveset unique to her weapon alone and not its type.
- A common internet meme surrounding the Revenant among the player base was using her to wield colossal weapons due to her stature. Notably, this might have been given an official nod in the form of one of the clones spawned during the Everdark Sovereign Libra fight being a Revenant wielding a great sword and great crusher.

sections.heading: Localization
sections.markdown:
- Although her english name is shared with the Royal Revenant (王族の幽鬼) enemy, her Japanese name, 復讐者, is different and was consistently translated as Revenger in the base game, such as Dragon Communion Revenger Ekzykes, Revenger's Shack, and Edgar the Revenger.
 - Interestingly, she does fight a Royal Revenant by the end of her Remembrance.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Red Letter** is an Info Item in Elden Ring. It is part of Tanith, Volcano Manor Proprietress's questline.

sections.heading: Use
sections.markdown:
- Use the **Red Letter** to read its full description.
- Unlocks the invasion sign of Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood near the Shack of the Lofty in the Mountaintops of the Giants, marking its location on the map. Defeating him awards Hoslow's Petal Whip, Hoslow's Set, Rune Arc ×1, and Furlcalling Finger Remedy ×1. Return to Tanith afterward to receive the Taker's Cameo and select "**See the Lord**" to be transported to the Audience Pathway.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Location**: Volcano Manor
- The **Red Letter** is found in the drawing room of Volcano Manor after Rileigh the Idle has been disposed of.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- This item cannot be sold, stored, or dropped.
- Max held: 1
- Even if this item is collected after defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, the task can still be completed and Tanith's reward will be placed where the Red Letter was found.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Radahn Soldier** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Soldiers in the service of General Radahn, reputed to be masterful warriors and rumoured to know no weakness. Their surcoats display the crest of a red-maned lion raising a sword in the image of Radahn, and their visors are styled after a lion's fangs.

They can be found throughout Caelid, fighting off the Scarlet Rot using torches and Fire Pots.

Blue, spectral Radahn Soldiers, akin to puppets, can be found in Fort Faroth.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Redmane Knight** is an enemy in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Knights in the service of General Radahn's Redmane army. They wear the crest of a red-maned lion on their armour and greatshields, and the red plumes on their helms symbolise Radahn's pedigree as the son of Radagon.

When they were driven to defeat by Malenia's Scarlet Rot, the Redmane Knights burned the crest on the left breast of their armour to indicate their resolve, knowing that their duty in Caelid would prevent them from seeing their homes again. They remained in Caelid, staving off the Rot using fire-based techniques, employing Redmane Fire Pots and igniting their own weapons.

The longest-serving Redmane Knight, Ogha, studied gravity-manipulating techniques alongside Radahn.

Spectral Redmane Knights can be found engaged in combat with spectral Cleanrot Knights in the War-Dead Catacombs.
